text: Everything that happens after the code.
A practical gathering for the people building what comes next.

text:
Opening: introduce Beyond Code 2027 as a practical gathering about the business, trust, communication and delivery that surround technology.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, page 1.
The work begins after the code.
A useful product still has to earn trust, reach people and make sense in the real world.

What makes people believe
a product will deliver?

How does good work find
the people who need it?

How do teams explain value,
price fairly and keep moving?
Everything that happens after the code.

Frame the event around the work that makes technology useful and sustainable: trust, clear communication, reach, pricing, marketing and delivery.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, pages 1–2.
A small, high-participation event for people doing the work across tech.

The proposal sets the event for Saturday 27 March 2027 in Ibadan, Oyo State, with the venue still to be confirmed. It lists 100 tech professionals, three guest speakers, three sessions, and an 8:30am–6:00pm programme.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, pages 1 and 4.
Three conversations with room to work.
Each session is built around real examples, audience participation and useful takeaways.
How Nigerians decide to trust and buy
Build a problem chosen by the room
Review, test and ship a feature live
Handle data, money and relationships fairly

Session 1 is intended for a brand, marketing or growth strategist and includes positioning, naira pricing, brand signals, social proof, distribution and an audit of three attendee products, pages or profiles. Session 2 is for a senior software engineer and includes a room-selected live build, AI tools, review/testing/shipping, plus local conditions such as patchy networks and local payments. Session 3 is for a founder, senior operator or consultant and covers client communication, proposals, pricing/timelines, data/money handling and fair relationships, with live rewrites and open questions.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, pages 3–4.
A day people can take part in.
The programme leaves space to meet, ask, try and compare notes.
Breaks and a dedicated open hour to meet collaborators.
Ship It Sprint · Tech Trivia · The Naira Test · Cracked Bingo
Collect questions and make space for people to show their work.
₦2,000 tickets · partner prizes first · live draw
Designed to feel like a gathering, not a row of presentations.

The proposal includes networking during breaks and an open hour; Ship It Sprint, Tech Trivia, The Naira Test and Cracked Bingo; a question board; demo corner; and a laptop raffle. Raffle details: tickets are ₦2,000, sold at check-in and through the day, numbered and linked to each buyer, with partner prizes awarded before the live draw.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, pages 4–5.
A focused room, with a real reason to be there.
Bring your point of view to people who are building, selling and supporting technology.
Short talks, live work and open Q&A—not a 45-minute slide run.
Professional photos, video clips, social feature and speaker spotlight.
Find peers, possible collaborators, clients and future hires.
Share what succeeded, what failed and what others can use.

The proposal describes an audience of 100 tech professionals and emphasizes short talks/live work/Q&A, professional photos and video clips, a social feature and speaker spotlight, and meeting engineers, designers, founders, marketers and potential collaborators, clients or hires.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, page 5.
Practical by design. Supported by the team.
A clear brief and thoughtful logistics make it easier to bring your best work.
Bring the work behind the work.
Real examples, numbers, stories and mistakes
No more than 10 slides; teach rather than pitch
Stay for questions and the networking hour
Transport support or honorarium, agreed individually
Lodging for speakers travelling from outside Ibadan
Clear brief and a 30-minute prep call

The requested style is grounded: examples, numbers, stories and mistakes; maximum 10 slides; teach rather than pitch; stay for Q&A and networking. The organizers offer transport support or an individually agreed honorarium, lodging for speakers outside Ibadan, reserved seating, meals/refreshments, photos/video, a speaker spotlight, a clear brief and a 30-minute prep call.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, pages 5–6.
A clear timeline, from invitation to clips.
The team will help you prepare well ahead of the event.
A 30-minute call in early March gets the session aligned before final materials are due.

Timeline from the proposal: invitations in November–December 2026; confirmations by Friday 15 January 2027; announcements in January–February; prep call in early March; final slides/materials by Saturday 20 March; event on Saturday 27 March; session clips released in April.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, page 7.

Bring your
experience to
the room.
Availability for an early-March prep call
EMAIL + PHONE / WHATSAPP CONTACT DETAILS TO BE ADDED BEFORE SENDING

Invite the prospective speaker to reply with: an approximately 80-word bio, a high-resolution headshot, their session angle, and availability for a 30-minute prep call in early March. The source proposal uses [Email] and [Phone or WhatsApp] placeholders; these details must be filled in before the deck is sent.
Source: Beyond-Code-2027-Speaker-Proposal.pdf, page 8.
